Annual Day and 2019 Batch Graduation Ceremony Held at MGIMS
Monday, 15 September 2025
2581 Hits
Sevagram, September 13, 2025 — The Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, celebrated its Foundation and Annual Day on September 13, 2025, at the New Auditorium on its campus. Dr. Pankaj Kanchan Rajesh Bhoyar, Hon’ble State Minister, Government of Maharashtra for Home (Rural), Housing, School Education, Co-operatives, Mining, and Guardian Minister for Wardha and Bhandara Districts, served as the Chief Guest. Shri PL Tapadiya (President, Kasturba Health Society), Dr BS Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr Poonam Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital) and Dr Satish Kumar (Officer In-Charge, Student Council) were also present on the dias. The event also marked the graduation ceremony of the MBBS 2019 batch and was attended by students, faculty, staff, alumni, and parents.
The Chief Guest, Dr. Bhoyar, distributed awards to meritorious undergraduate and postgraduate students in recognition of their academic excellence and extracurricular achievements. Hospital staff and community health workers were also honoured for their dedicated service to the institution. Graduation certificates were then awarded to the MBBS 2019 batch students, marking a significant milestone in their journey as healthcare professionals.
Following his felicitation, Dr. Bhoyar delivered the keynote address, acknowledging MGIMS as a premier institute committed to rural healthcare and holistic medical education. He said,
“Sevagram Hospital holds a special place in each of our hearts. It is truly ‘our hospital’—a place we deeply love and respect. While we may sometimes point out its shortcomings, our faith in the institution and its values remains committed.”
Addressing the graduating class, he added, "
The path ahead will not always be easy. But no matter where life takes you, always remain true to the ethics, values, and honesty that you have imbibed from this hallowed institution. These principles will be your guiding light in the most challenging moments of your journey.”
A heartfelt reflection was delivered by Dr. Satyanarayani and Dr. Aditya Tripathi, representatives of the MBBS 2019 batch. They spoke about their transformative journey at MGIMS, shared nostalgic memories, and expressed gratitude for the mentorship and opportunities provided by the institute.
The program continued with an address by Shri P. L. Tapdiya, President of the Kasturba Health Society. He reaffirmed the Society’s commitment to strengthening medical education and research at MGIMS. He emphasized the importance of community-oriented care and encouraged the young doctors to uphold the values instilled by the institute.
“This day is not an end but the beginning of a lifelong journey of service, compassion, and responsibility. As you step out into the world as doctors, remember that your true education begins now—in the wards, in the villages, and in the lives of the people you touch,”
he said.
Dr. A.K. Shukla extended his best wishes to the graduating batch, expressing hope that they achieve all they have aspired for in both their personal and professional lives. The Hippocratic Oath was administered by Dr. Dilip Gupta, President of the Alumni Association and Head of the Department of Surgery. The solemn ceremony marked a defining moment for the graduating students as they pledged to uphold the highest standards of medical ethics, compassion, and integrity in their professional lives.
Dr. Satish Kumar presented the formal introduction of the Chief Guest, Dr. Pankaj Bhoyar. Dr. Abhay Deshmukh (Associate Professor of Pathology) and Ms. Anoushka Sakpal (Undergraduate Student, Batch of 2021) conducted the program. The event concluded with the National Anthem.
